title: Operations around the model: discovery, capture reading, proof and delivery (job and C# feature), authorization and publication, development data, reference refresh, Studio session, ODC Portal APIs, debugger, environment checks and the common diagnostic taxonomy; contracts of the existing public entries only (nothing here executes, logs in, publishes or writes external data)

capabilities.title: Contextual discovery: from an intent to the capabilities, contracts, examples, evidence and gaps of the lane
capabilities.summary: `ssam discover "<intent>" --lane <odc|o11> [--app <capture.oml>] [--budget <bytes>]` answers once, within a hard byte budget, with the matching capabilities (exact public operation, role and operation statements with evidence per lane), contract slices, example excerpts, bindings, dependencies, unavailable entries and the exact continuation; `--expand <id>:operations+native+contract+example+evidence` returns what the budget omitted; `--detail <id>` opens one capability. Read-only; it never executes, delivers or validates natively.

route.operation: ssam discover "<intent>" --lane <odc|o11> [--app <capture.oml>] [--budget N]; --expand <id>:<parts>; MCP ssam_discover {intent, lane, app?, expand?, detail?, type?, limit?, budgetBytes?}

capabilities.guidance: Name the element and the operation in the intent (e.g. 'rename the Email attribute of Contact'); read `focus`, `operations.<op>.roles.<role>.<lane>` (status + evidence) and `unavailable` before acting. `--app` takes a capture (.oml) only in isolated work; a module NAME talks to the live Studio. A status is declared by the catalog; the evidence (proven-current / proven-historical / declared-not-proven) is computed from the stamped results of this machine. Declared refusals (unavailable) are kept under any budget; a reduced answer names every reduced section with its exact --expand.

limits.text: The O11 index serves only the capabilities of the shared catalog; nothing is inherited from the ODC descriptor.

capabilities.title: Read an application capture: map, elements, properties, usages
capabilities.summary: Start with the module map: `ssam map` / MCP `ssam_map` answers from the module index of the capture (one file per capture sha256, kept across sessions) with every element, its @key, kind, role, parent and path, paged and filtered by kind, name, prefix, role or parent. Then the read-only reader over the same capture (.oml, reused by sha256) or, on ODC, an open module by name: kind/name/text queries with paging, a path or @key subtree with depth, usages for consumers, select for up to 32 paths in one call, a budget for the inline size (the full JSON is always written to `out`). Identities (keys, paths) are bound to the capture's sourceSha256; pass expectedSourceSha256 to refuse a changed capture.

route.operation: both, first: ssam map [--lane odc|o11] <capture.oml|Module> [--kind K] [--name N] [--prefix P] [--role R] [--parent @key] [--offset N] [--max N] [--budget B] [--detail] / MCP ssam_map {lane, target, kind?, name?, prefix?, role?, parent?, key?, offset?, max?, budgetBytes?, includeDetail?, expectedSourceSha256?}; ODC: odc inspect <capture.oml> [Kind:Name/...|@key] [--kind K] [--name N] [--text T] [--usages] [--select p ...] [--budget N] / MCP studio_inspect {target, path?, kind?, name?, text?, select?, usages?, depth?, max?, budget?, expectedSourceSha256?}; O11: ssam inspect --lane o11 --oml <capture.oml> [--kind K] [--name N] [--text T] [--path P|@key] [--select ...] [--depth N] [--max N]; both: ssam discover --app <capture.oml>

capabilities.guidance: To read an application, start with ssam map / ssam_map; then inspect subtrees, properties and usages by @key with the expected sha256 (the map's continuations carry both). ok=true means the query ran, not that the answer is complete: check notices, kindObserved, searchComplete and omissions. Kinds are interface names without the leading I (MobileScreen, ServerAction...). Reuse the same capture between pages; after any Studio change take a new capture (keys are not valid across captures). Cross-cutting questions (where a site property, a variable or a text is used, who calls an action, the impact of a change, usages across the modules of an app) are ONE ssam_map call: view search {text, regex?, property?, kind?, role?} or view uses {element}, with target one capture or the list of the app's modules. A module name as target snapshots the live module first (ODC); in isolated work use .oml captures only.

limits.text: Schema limits: select <= 32, depth <= 12, max <= 500, budget 2000..200000; above the budget the answer carries navigation.target and the hash instead of the body.
The reader needs the local Anvil authority key (bridge.key) and may build the builder once; each inspect writes a journal line with the capture file and its sourceSha256.

The module map (view map) covers the reader-visible elements (names, kinds, roles, parents, data types of parameters, attributes and variables); text search, property values, usages and other modules are the views search and uses, over the rich index of each capture, built only when one of them asks (rich ensure). A missing index is built once by the lane reader (index ensure) and a stale or corrupt one is never served.
O11 reads go through the kernel reader of the lane (kernel-reading.mjs) and journal in .local/reading/operations.jsonl; captures only (no live-module target).

The module map (view map) covers the reader-visible elements (names, kinds, roles, parents, data types of parameters, attributes and variables); text search, property values, usages and other modules are the views search and uses, over the rich index of each capture, built only when one of them asks (rich ensure). A missing index is built once by the lane reader (index ensure) and a stale or corrupt one is never served.

capabilities.title: Deliver a job to the open module directly (a fixture proof only when asked), with receipts and reconciliation
capabilities.summary: Deliver directly, no proof or preview first. Delivery, ODC: `studio_deliver {feature, module, job, owners, changes}` captures the open module as it is now, applies the job privately on that capture, writes the manifest (a change against the capture, read element by element; NO_CHANGE when there is none), then check-base, preview and merge (strictlyEqual), refusing before any change; it never publishes; `until` stops earlier (snapshot|build|check-base|preview) only when the person asks to review. Proof, only when the person asks: `ssam job --lane <odc|o11> <job.json>` applies the job headless on the declared base (Verify + expected messages) and delivers nothing (MCP ssam_job / o11_job). Delivery, O11: `o11_deliver {module, job, checks, authorize}` (merge in Service Studio; publishing is `o11_publish {module, authorize}` with the user's words), or the O11 session tools context/propose/continue/status. The steps are also public one by one: studio_manifest {base, candidate, output, feature, owners, changes} (needs the base capture identity <base>.oml.json; refuses a changed hash, a missing host/developerId, an old capture, a foreign author), then studio_check_base / studio_preview / studio_merge {manifest}.

route.operation: ODC: odc deliver <feature> --job <job.json> --module <M> --owners '["Owner"]' --changes '["Change"]' / MCP studio_deliver; O11: ssam deliver --lane o11 --module <M> --job <job> --checks <names> / MCP o11_deliver; proof only when asked: ssam job --lane <lane> <job.json>; step by step: studio_manifest {base, candidate, output, feature, owners, changes} -> studio_check_base {manifest} -> studio_preview {manifest} -> studio_merge {manifest}

capabilities.guidance: Headless proof is not delivery evidence; a merge receipt with merged=true and strictlyEqual=true is. Refusal vocabulary of the ODC bridge (gate): base_drift (take a new snapshot and rebuild), candidate_validation (fix the job), equivalence (a merge is pending in the Studio: never repeat), known_losses (outcome incomplete: merged except the named defaults or delete rules; the continuation delivers the repair job, never the original again), authorship / provider_state / pending_match / scope / key_not_found (read the gate text), studio_busy (dismiss the dialog by caption), retry_refused (a started merge exists), uncertain (the native operation was handed off: read receipt.json / last-error.json / the journal and reconcile; NEVER retry). A job with expectValid:false is never deliverable. When the change cannot be written as a job (new module, producer dependency, reparenting, pattern widgets from a reference), ODC has the C# feature route (deliver.feature).

limits.text: studio_deliver requires module, owners and changes with a job, and forbids producer/tenant with a job; the kernel CLI must report flowLayoutEngine anvil-d4d8ece or delivery refuses; an existing output directory is refused (one directory per attempt).

Uncertain outcome: the job path marks `uncertain` when merged&&strictlyEqual is missing or the merge threw; the merge writes merge-started.json and refuses a repeat (retry_refused); a HandedOff native call or a 15-minute timeout is `uncertain` (merge-late line). Reconcile by receipt, never by repeating.

Both delivery paths answer `uncertain` when the Studio step throws during the merge (the result may have been applied: reconcile by receipt and journal, never retry); a throw before the merge is a plain failure with nothing merged. The deliver-job journal line keeps outcome, gate, failed stage and evidence directory.

The O11 lane merges and stops; publishing is a separate call, `o11_publish {module, authorize}`, with the user's own words (TrueChange errors come back and nothing is published). The O11 session tools keep a `reconcile` state when the write outcome is unknown; propose asks the user to accept the contract by elicitation, in the same process.

capabilities.title: C# feature route (Authoring primitives) for what jobs cannot express
capabilities.summary: An IFeature in platforms/odc/studio/builder/features using the Authoring/AuthoringData/AuthoringUi/AuthoringMisc/AuthoringRest primitives; `odc build list` shows the registered features; `odc build <feature> <base.oml> <sha> <dir> [--producer <oml>] --smoke` proves headless (a new directory; any new warning is refused); `odc deliver <feature>` runs the same gates as jobs. Required for: a new module (builder new + studio_create with createAuthorization), AddDependency with --producer, reparenting (IModelServices.MoveObject), widgets from a reference WidgetDefinition, native Copy of producer nodes.

route.operation: write features/<Name>.cs, dotnet build studio/builder, odc build list, odc build <feature> <base.oml> <sha> <dir> --smoke, odc deliver <feature> --until preview / MCP studio_build, studio_deliver

capabilities.guidance: Model API reference for C#: platforms/odc/docs/model-api/INDEX.md (reflection; the ODC Studio version is recorded there). Creating a new module asset (studio_create) writes revision 1 on the tenant without deploying and requires the user's own createAuthorization words; a create-started marker refuses a repeat; reconcile an uncertain create with studio_assets.

limits.text: Live-merged proofs of the feature route are receipts in platforms/odc/lab/<dir>/evidence of the operational checkout; they are not part of this index.
The builder refuses any new warning; Data Actions take no inputs; the native Button Group cannot be authored.

alternatives.when: a job can express the change: jobs are proven on the fixture and need no C# compile

capabilities.title: Authorize and publish (the user's own words), with the publish receipt and reconciliation
capabilities.summary: After a merge receipt (or a create receipt), `odc studio authorize <manifest> publish "<the user's own words>"` records the authorization in the manifest and `odc studio publish <manifest> --wait` publishes natively, compares the open model with the receipt and downloads the published revision (publish-receipt.json: state, revision, sha256, matchesOpenModule, strictlyEqual). Publication is never automatic and never retried after an uncertain result.

route.operation: studio_authorize {manifest, kind:"publish", text:"<user words>"} then studio_publish {manifest, wait:true, minutes?}

capabilities.guidance: The text must be the user's own words, quoted, not a paraphrase (the bridge only checks it is not empty; the MCP schema requires at least 8 characters). A merge receipt outcome `MergeAndPublish` is a native label and does not mean a publication happened (publishInvoked says). A publish-started.json marker refuses any repeat ('never republish'); an uncertain publish is reconciled with studio_command publish-status (publish-status.json), studio_wait published <M> and studio_latest, never by publishing again. The same studio_authorize with kind "create" records the createAuthorization of a new module asset (deliver.feature).

limits.text: studio_publish requires publishAuthorization, a receipt with ok and merged or created, the open model equal to the receipt hash (or the MatchTree for a created module), no native errors and the expected revision when declared.
studio_authorize needs the live Studio (the command goes through the bridge).
studio_publish accepts minutes up to 30, but the bridge stops waiting on `publish --wait` after 20 minutes and answers uncertain (studio_busy): reconcile, never republish.

depends.unless: the merge or create receipt came from the feature route (deliver.feature): publication needs a receipt, whichever route produced it

capabilities.title: Read or write records of the development database (not a model change)
capabilities.summary: ODC: the Studio's own data service (View/Edit data) on an entity of the open module: studio_data {module, entity, limit?, offset?, fields?} reads; studio_data_insert|update|delete write only with the user's authorization words. O11: o11_data, Edit Data through the Service Studio connected on the O11 lane with its own login (SSO included; host only checks its environment); writes declare an authorization and an operationId.

route.operation: ODC: odc studio data <Module> <Entity> [--limit N]; data-insert|data-update --records-file <journal/data/requests/x.json> --authorize "<words>"; data-delete --ids ... --authorize / MCP studio_data*; O11: MCP o11_data {request}

capabilities.guidance: Business data is not model data: a catalog task never writes records by itself. Corporate tenants only on explicit instruction. Receipts: journal/data/<ts>-<Entity>-<op>.json (ODC).

limits.text: Reading is proven live; inserts/updates/deletes have no receipt in the repository (HANDOFF 'P sem prova').

Known gap: ODC data writes have no start marker nor operationId: a partial write (some records failed) throws after writing and is journaled gate_refused, another native exception is native_error, and only a 3-minute timeout becomes uncertain, so an interrupted write cannot be reconciled by receipt.

O11 writes are reconciled by receipt: the request needs the user's authorization words and a stable UUID operationId; a receipt is written `pending` before the call and `completed` after; the same operationId with another request is refused, a `pending` receipt refuses any new request until reconciled, and a `completed` one is replayed instead of writing again.

capabilities.title: Refresh the references of an open module in the live Studio, with the refresh receipt
capabilities.summary: studio_refresh_references {module, producer?} (CLI `odc studio refresh-references <M> [--producer <Lib|key>]`) refreshes the references of the open module in the live Studio, optionally of one producer; the receipt journal/refresh-<M>-<stamp>.json|.txt records mode, changed, sha256Before/After, dependenciesBefore/After, refreshedReferences and differencesOutsideReferences.
capabilities.guidance: This is a Studio write on the open module (not headless). It refuses with a modal dialog open, a pending merge, a logged-out session, or a producer the module does not reference. Read the receipt before any further step; after a refresh take a new snapshot before delivering (the base changed).

limits.text: Known gap: no start marker, no repeat guard and no HandedOff marking: a refusal after the mutation (the final requirement check runs after the receipt is written) is journaled gate_refused and a native exception native_error, never uncertain; only a 5-minute timeout is uncertain. Reconcile with the receipt and a new snapshot, never by repeating blindly.

capabilities.title: Studio session operations: status, attach, wait, open/close, dialogs, snapshot/latest, assets, consumers, create asset
capabilities.summary: studio_status / studio_doctor read; studio_attach loads the bridge DLL into the running Studio; studio_open {module, localOml?} / studio_close {module, duplicates?, discard?} change the open modules; studio_wait {condition: idle|no-dialogs|published|open, timeoutSeconds} blocks at most 20 minutes in the bridge (the schema accepts 1800 s; beyond 20 minutes the answer is uncertain/studio_busy); studio_dismiss_dialog {caption, action} clicks a dialog button; studio_snapshot {module} writes snapshots/<M>-<sha>.oml(+.json identity); studio_latest downloads the server revision; studio_assets lists assets of the tenant; studio_consumers lists the modules that consume one; studio_command passes any bridge command through (its own gates still apply).
capabilities.guidance: These act on the user's running ODC Studio and tenant session: never use them for isolated catalog work. A snapshot is idempotent by hash (never overwritten) and is the identity every read and delivery binds to. studio_close with discard keeps a -discarded snapshot first. studio_open trims the module name at the first space (a module name with spaces is not opened by name). The annotations readOnlyHint on snapshot/latest/assets/consumers/inspect/check_base/preview hide that they write local files.

limits.text: studio_open with an unconfirmed result answers 'do not retry blindly'; studio_open splits the name at the first space.
Module resolution cascades: open modules, the tenant catalog section, any section, snapshots/*.json, then ObjectKey.Parse; there is no explicit not-found answer; an asset name is not a module name.

studio_consumers writes snapshots/<M>-consumers.json although annotated read-only; the bridge answers any command still running after its timeout (merge 15, publish --wait 20, wait 20 minutes) as uncertain/studio_busy and does not cancel it.

capabilities.title: Portal public APIs: operation catalog, read calls (deployments, build feedback, environments), write policy
capabilities.summary: odc_status, odc_list_apis, odc_search_operations {apiId?, search?, readOnly?}, odc_describe_operation {operationId} and odc_portal_capabilities/odc_describe_capability are local catalog reads; odc_read {operationId, path?, query?} calls a read operation of the tenant with the API Client credential of the vault (deployments _Filter/_Get/_GetMessages, build feedback, environments). odc_write is registered only with an exact allowlist policy per tenant (none today).
capabilities.guidance: Discovering an operation in the catalog is not an authenticated integration nor a write authorization. Reads retry once on 401 and never on 429; local quota 100/min per API (10/min for environment-configurations-api-v1). Errors are coded (INPUT_INVALID, OPERATION_NOT_FOUND, AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED, API_UNAUTHORIZED, API_FORBIDDEN, WRITE_BLOCKED, LOCAL_RATE_LIMIT, NETWORK_ERROR...) with location and retrySafety. Runtime logs and traces are not served by the facade (odc_portal_read exists only in the ODC3 host).

limits.text: odc_write is not registered while every tenant has policyFile=null; its MCP schema has no authorization field (the CLI requires --authorize); no reconciliation tool exists for a write.
The MCP odc_read writes no journal line (the CLI does); monitoring answers carry liveVerified:false.

capabilities.title: Headless debugger: scenarios, breakpoints, runtime trace, variables and stepping
capabilities.summary: ssam_debug {op: start|watch|status|stop|variables|continue|step-over|step-into|step-out, lane, module, moduleKey, runtimeUrl, nodeKeys[1..20 without trace; 1..200 with trace or watch], trace (optional trace window), tenant (ODC), o11Auth (optional native SSO metadata), seconds, pauseSeconds, autoContinue, paths, frame, depth, threadId, eventId}: one debugger session per target, manifest/receipt under .local/debugger/<sessionId>, a lock per target; status and stop answer from the receipt. Start/watch opens an English native Username/Password window, with platform/application in its title and environment in its body; secrets never belong in arguments. Watch waits for external app use, invokes nothing and declares request isolation and app-request identity unproved.

route.operation: ssam debug prepare|run|status --request <json-file> / MCP ssam_debug_run; native-entry default on both lanes; ssam_debug remains the server-session tool; explicit legacy rest-wrapper for release/reconcile; read-only lock inventory: ssam debug locks [--lane o11|odc] / MCP ssam_debug_run op:locks; ssam_debug_invoke and execution:rest-wrapper are LEGACY (not interactive, not counted); interactive inspection: ssam_debug_server / ssam_debug_client (CLI ssam debug server|client --stdio); final matrix (req 19): ssam debug matrix [--check] / MCP ssam_debug_matrix (read-only; generated from platforms/odc/facade/debug-matrix/matrix-source.json, writes only .local/debugger/final-matrix/matrix.json|md; --check exits 1 on drift, including a pointer doc without its marker; git HEAD is reported, not hashed); bounded frame read: ssam_debug_server op read-frame (maxNodes default 2000, cap 20000; continuations nextOffset and pending) and ssam_debug op read-frame (CLI --max-nodes); whole-frame traversal: ssam_debug_server / ssam_debug_client op read-scope (maxNodes cap 20000, budget-omitted leaves, stale stop refuses); O11 reconcile by evidence class with verify:true (ssam_debug_server op reconcile)

capabilities.guidance: Debug ODC/O11 actions through original published entries, as the signed-in app user. New run/prepare/status requests default to execution=native-entry: no wrapper and no publication. The code selects the entry by breadth-first caller search, fixed kind priority and model key; entry overrides must be reachable. Complete hash-bound reads are required; a cut graph is refused. prepare reads the deployed revision and public assets, reports entry/path, typed input bindings, effect evidence and required acknowledgements without login or action execution. run opens the private App User Sign In window, then executes scenarios serially in an isolated Node host using original generated callables. Supported adapters: native server stubs, data actions and client actions; server/library/service targets need a verified consumer route. Direct REST/SOAP, timers/processes, arbitrary screen lifecycle and navigation remain unsupported. An unreachable private action reports dead code: no public entry reaches <action>. Fields: lane odc|o11, action name or @key, inputs or scenarios [{name,inputs}], trace none|nodes|full and optional window. ODC needs tenant/module; acknowledgeEffects must include each reported effect, including unknown-call for an unread producer. O11 needs host/module/moduleKey/applicationKey/runtimeUrl; modules adds captured producers. Trace requires observing the target and terminal server thread; missing evidence is not success. Native login, real permissions and cross-action identity propagation are separate proofs; connection or preparation does not prove access. Cross-module O11 redaction is an internal same-origin credential filter, not authorization. DEV only; a breakpoint may catch another user request, so request isolation remains unproved. Uncertain executions stop the batch and retain the binding lock. status reads receipts; never replay uncertain requests. Credentials only in the private window. execution=rest-wrapper explicitly selects legacy ODC publication behavior; release/reconcile address old leases. Current live proof coverage and restrictions: docs/DEBUGGER-HEADLESS-FALTA.md. Wave 2 (implemented, live proof pending): read-frame reads a whole frame in one native EvaluateMany plus one batch per tree level; ODC library-reference runs may carry consumer- and library-owned breakpoints in one library-keyed session (nodeModuleKeys; whether the runtime honours the consumer-owned id is unproved, .local/debugger/odc-library-breakpoint-contract/findings.json); an ODC start whose read-only preflight fails before StartDebugSession is refused, lock-free and not uncertain; O11 Timer without a REST/SOAP caller: ssam_debug_server run trigger service-center-run-now (one Run Now, no request hold, debugger stopped before the read-only Service Center correlation); O11 contextMode endpoint-credential for REST Custom and SOAP WebServiceMethod literal request-header checks (ODC Custom stays refused: no qualified request-header API inside ODC OnAuthentication); O11 Traditional screen-action postbacks (Submit and the original OsAjax request) and block Preparations; runner-derived O11 REST/SOAP callback scopes; ssam_debug_client start.pauseOnExceptions with pause.reason exception and a redacted type; per-runtime scope categories (notApplicableToRuntime, emptyInModel, notEnumerated); ODC mounted navigate {screen,back:true} and initial deep links with Text/Integer/LongInteger screen inputs; debugger private state under %USERPROFILE%\.ssam-hybrid\debugger (SSAM_DEBUG_STATE_ROOT overrides; legacy %LOCALAPPDATA%\SSAM copies, MSIX package stores included, are read only and reported per origin; cleanup claims hold across every store). Wave 3, all implemented, live proof pending: read-scope on ssam_debug_client and ssam_debug_server reads every root of the observed frame to its leaves in one command (children pages of 150, text pages, budget-omitted leaves; complete only when runtimeValuesComplete and no budget stopped it; a stale stop refuses the whole read); ODC ssam_debug_server run trigger portal-wake (native-background, words, trace full, no launch/inputs/workflow) binds the Timer scope before the single reserved Portal POST; ODC Timer and Workflow runs need a request-bound ThreadEnd for ok, and ODC Timer runs correlate the instance read-only in a separate Portal developer session (instanceCorrelation, executionCompleted, outcome, wakeOwnershipProved); ODC app-user anchor for private-compare anchor app-user, registered only after the original login proves identityMatches; producer End/response parity reported as counts only (End-stop capture not wired yet, so complete stays false); ODC mounted run.interactions [{target, event:click}] (one journaled trusted CDP click each, handlerInvoked null, handlerObserved from a native stop) and the read-only SDK error path (debug_odc_native_mount_lifecycle_exception, debug_odc_native_mount_error_page_observed); scopesFrom mount-lifecycle also covers the navigation target handlers; ODC REST callback scopes (OnAuthentication Basic/Custom, OnRequest/OnResponse, OnBeforeRequest/OnAfterResponse of consumed RestActions toward the app origin only; debug_odc_native_callback_scope_not_derived) and ODC Settings in category setting; contextMode endpoint-credential on both lanes for original endpoint entries: header scheme (O11 Custom, O11 SOAP header check, REST None with a literal OnRequest/method header guard) and basic scheme (qualified ODC Basic, O11 developer-logic Basic; O11 Basic with one platform User_Login stays app-user), scheme taken from the published capability only; InternalAccess=Yes refused before any GET (debug_native_endpoint_internal_access_only, platformRestriction), client-certificate and exposed OAuth2 typed refusals; O11 reconcile by evidence class (answered, confirmed-not-started archived to reconciled-prestart.lock, login-refusal; verify:true re-reads a prestart archive) and the O11 client aborted reconcile (zero business submissions only, reconciled-client-aborted.lock, executionOutcome aborted-unconfirmed); locks retained by user decision (RETAINED_LOCKS: the SSAMDebuggerProbe Timer wake 60aa32e5, a Timer wake, not a BPT launch) are refused by every reconcile, archive and neutralization with debug_lock_retained_by_decision; O11 Timer wake failures use debug_native_background_timer_* and BPT keeps debug_native_background_bpt_*; O11 BPT activity roots from the native scope (categories by owner key, launch bindings by key; valuesComplete stays false until interactive BPT inspection); ODC Process-like kinds are refused as not in the ODC product (debug_native_background_odc_bpt_not_in_product). Identity and role witnesses (debug-identity-witness.mjs) are trusted only when their published assignment is natively bound to GetUserId()/NullIdentifier() or the pinned role Check<Role>Role (roleKey + roleModuleKey), pinned by sourceSha256; name matches are never accepted; this qualifier is not wired into the sessions yet.

Live-qualified on MCP (CLI proof pending): Library producer frames; REST anonymous. Not interactive, refused with the code shown: REST Basic (debug_native_endpoint_basic_credentials_unavailable_after_odc_srp); REST Custom authentication (debug_native_endpoint_custom_authentication_unqualified); Workflow event (debug_odc_native_server_inspection_entry_required). capabilities.title: Diagnose a failure: common outcome/gate taxonomy, Verify messages, locating the element, proven cause vs hypothesis, reconciliation of uncertain writes
capabilities.summary: Outcomes: ok | gate_refused | native_error | uncertain (the native operation was already handed off). ODC bridge gates: base_drift, equivalence, known_losses, authorship, provider_state, pending_match, studio_busy, key_not_found, scope, candidate_validation, retry_refused, none. Kernel Verify (job results): validation.{new, fixed, preexisting, unexpected, missingExpected, ambiguous, tolerated}, accepted, isValid, each message with {id, type, key, path, detail} where key = [msgId, objectKey, [props], [messageParameters]] and path = 'Module (ESpace) / X (ServerAction) / ...'. Portal errors are coded (OdcError {code, message, location, issues, status, retryAfterSeconds, retrySafety}); the debugger and friction records carry their own codes.

route.operation: read the answer's outcome/gate/validation; locate with ssam discover --app <capture> --expand element:<Kind:Name|@key> or studio_inspect <capture> <path>; reconcile uncertain writes by their receipts (receipt.json, last-error.json, publish-status.json, refresh-*.json, journal/operations.jsonl); the Verify message key is built in kernel/src/Anvil.Core/Kernel/ModelHost.cs:215-216

capabilities.guidance: Hints distinguish a proven cause from a hypothesis: the native Verify message, a gate refusal and a coded Portal error are facts; the gate classification of the bridge is a substring heuristic (unmatched = none) and friction codes are regex classifications: say so when relying on them. A key locates an element only inside the capture it came from (sourceSha256); after reopening or changing the module, locate again by Kind:Name. When the platform gives no location, say that the location is absent and return the best evidence (message text, module path) without inventing precision. Never 'fix' by changing target or environment, repeating an uncertain merge/publish/create/refresh/data write, or disabling validation: an uncertain write is reconciled by receipt, then decided by the user.

limits.text: Bridge refusals carry no structured location (the hint is in the text); key_not_found is missing from the README refusal tables.
ModelPath answers suggestions (the name exists in another kind, similar names) or the candidate list when ambiguous.
The O11 session tools keep `reconcile` when the write state is unknown; job results use the same Verify validation categories as ODC.
